The fact of the matter is that a binary system is the simplest and easiest to use. Sometimes simple is better, even if we could conceive of other ways of doing things.

A policy of collecting anonymous information about "like" or "dislike" makes it easier for political groups to manufacture consensus. It would incentivize factions to game this system in order to convert others to their subjective point of view or political position, by making a position seem more popular or less popular than it really was.

I would strongly encourage the site to instead adopt a culture where comments are upvoted for the time, effort, and thought they took to produce. I would strongly discourage it from collecting any information simply about "agree" or "disagree".

Even when we disagree with the conclusions of an individual post, a cultural of upvoting based on effort rather than agreeableness will increase the long term likehood that counterarguments will appear which repudiate that which we disagree with. That is, when commenters know that their argument will not be suppressed based on popularity, and know that they stand a chance of gaining an audience based on the degree of effort they contributed to the post, they will be more likely to take the time raising a counter-argument repudiating the initial argument which was disagreeable.

I believe that it will ultimately be informative and valuable to users, to work towards a site which aggregates well thought out arguments and counter-arguments, then it is to develop a site which simply collects anonymous data concerning popularity, where the validity and integrity of such data is impossible to verify in an anonymous setting.

This subverse was created to provide an informative and unbiased setting for photographers and photographic artists to improve upon their technique and creative application. We are only accepting photographic submissions right now and each submission must be 80% photography to qualify -if you add a bit of paint or pencil to a bit for effect that's fine but it still should be a mostly photographic medium.

Submissions

  • Submissions must be of your own work. Do not submit found images or works not of your own making.
  • When asking for a critique, give a brief artist statement or some background information on the piece and your history in art so we can better personalize your critique.
  • If you're interested in knowing what people might think the concept is then include that in your intro comment and update us when someone has deciphered your message or if you didn't have a specific message.
  • There will be both technical (exposure, composition, Photoshop application, etc.) and creative (concept, story line, how the image translates emotionally) criticism welcomed here. If you are only interested in one, make that known.
  • Be prepared for negative feedback; there might be the common theme of suggesting you scrap the concept or re-shoot it. These suggestions are made with the idea to improve, if the feedback says the image will bring down your portfolio or aesthetic then you might wish to look at the work and conduct a self analysis on the how and why it could/should be improved.
  • Do not post with the intent of gaining exposure or requesting "likes".

Critics

  • When offering criticism include technique and creative suggestions for improvement.
  • We are looking at the image, not critiquing the model's (if it applies) appearance. If there's a technical issue with the model's posing that can be improved upon for the photographer's reference in the future as the authority figure on the image then it can be included.

Example of what to do: "Be mindful of posing your model's elbows as they can distort the shape of the arm in an unflattering manner." Example of what NOT to do: "You chose an ugly model, those elbows are all wrinkled making this photo horrible."

  • If the submitter requests a specific critique or questions a specific area of improvement, refrain from commenting on other aspects of the image.
  • If the subject matter offends you or ignites a passionate response take a step back and consider not commenting. We are looking for neutral criticism to improve the technical and creative approach to photography.

EduReads

  • Is there a book or website you've found that has greatly improved your photographic technique? Share the knowledge and post links with a brief description.
  • DO NOT repeatedly post the same referrals. Repeat material within a short time-frame (1-2 weeks) will be removed.
  • DO NOT post your own edu material with referral links on where to buy.

The forum is open to improve upon this sticky! If you have any suggestions on how to improve the text already applied or additions/subtractions to make voice them here. This is to be a community that facilitates a positive constructive critique.

You don't have to love the piece but do not call it trash either. Understand that someone put the time and effort to create something they loved and believed in and want to make the next image better and they're asking for your help.
